findings.source_quote: However, the church, can forget of that life, / If the presence of God, shines as the sun, / The singing so sweet, includes everyone.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace these lines with: “Tog kan die kerk daardie lewe vergeet, / as God se teenwoordigheid soos die son skyn, / en die sang so lieflik is dat almal deelneem.” This preserves the source’s conditional “If” and the claim that the singing includes everyone.
findings.translation_quote: Tog kan die kerk daardie lewe vergeet, / As God se teenwoordigheid soos die son skyn, / Is die sang so lieflik dat almal daarby inskakel.

findings.source_quote: Would we lose our life, for the good Lord’s sake? / Then eternity we’d gain, and heaven partake. / Or love our life, which the Bible is clear / We’d lose our chance, at heaven so dear.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace with: “Sou ons ons lewe ter wille van die goeie Here verloor? / Dan sou ons die ewigheid wen en deel hê aan die hemel. / Of sou ons ons lewe liefhê? Die Bybel stel dit duidelik: / Ons sou ons kans op die kosbare hemel verloor.” The source contrasts losing one’s life for the Lord with loving one’s life; it does not say to lay down one’s life.
findings.translation_quote: Sou ons ons lewe ter wille van die goeie Here aflê? / Dan sou ons die ewigheid wen en deel hê aan die hemel. / Of het ons ons lewe lief, terwyl die Bybel dit duidelik stel: / Ons sou ons kans op die kosbare hemel verloor.

findings.source_quote: When the next life is heaven, eternity with Him, / Then death is the beginning, so why is it grim?
findings.suggested_fix: Replace with: “As die volgende lewe die hemel is, die ewigheid saam met Hom, / Dan is die dood die begin—waarom is dit dan somber?” The source asks why death is grim; “donker” changes the sense to dark.
findings.translation_quote: As die volgende lewe die hemel is, die ewigheid saam met Hom, / Dan is die dood die begin—waarom is dit dan so donker?
